title: ‘Tell me what you see beyond dharma and adharma’
theme: Naciketas asks again: tell me what you see as other than dharma and adharma, other than what is made and unmade, other than what has been and what is to be.

words.context: Śaṅkara: «शास्त्रीयाद्धर्मानुष्ठानात्», the practice of scriptural duty, with its fruit and agents
Śaṅkara: «विहिताकरणरूपात् पापात्», sin, the failure to do what is enjoined

words.meaning: from the made and the unmade
words.context: Śaṅkara: «कृतं कार्यमकृतं कारणम्», effect and cause

sandhi.type: t voiced before a vowel; a + a
sandhi.rule: dharmāt and adharmāt become -d before a vowel, P. 8.2.39 (झलां जशोऽन्ते); anyatra + adharmāt and anyatra + asmāt join long, P. 6.1.101 (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः).
t becomes c before c, P. 8.4.40 (स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः).

sandhi.type: t voiced before a voiced consonant

samasa.meaning: the made and the unmade, taken together (hence singular)

morphology.note: Adverb ‘elsewhere’, here construed with the ablative: ‘other than, apart from’. It is repeated four times.
Gerundive of √bhū used as a noun: ‘what is to be’, the future.
The present of √dṛś is formed from the stem paśya-.

translation.literal: Other than dharma, other than adharma, other than this made-and-unmade, other than what has been and what is to be — that which you see, tell that.
translation.readable: Tell me what you see that is beyond right and wrong, beyond what is made and unmade, beyond what has been and what is still to be.

anvaya: धर्मात् अन्यत्र, अधर्मात् अन्यत्र, अस्मात् कृताकृतात् अन्यत्र, भूतात् च भव्यात् च अन्यत्र यत् तत् पश्यसि, तत् वद ।
syntax: A request in one sentence. Four phrases of anyatra with an ablative describe the object (yat tat) of paśyasi; the imperative vada, with tad picking up the relative, closes it. The phrases are not joined by ca, so whether they describe one object or several is a question the commentators argue.

ambiguities.note: Śaṅkara: one thing, beyond all that can be dealt with — beyond rites with their fruit and means, beyond effect and cause, beyond the three times: «कालत्रयेण यन्न परिच्छिद्यत इत्यर्थः». Raṅgarāmānuja reports Vyāsārya’s reading, given under Brahmasūtra 1.4.6, that three things are asked: the means («धर्मः उपायः» — a means unlike the familiar ones, «प्रसिद्धोपायविलक्षण उपायः इत्यर्थः»), the goal («प्रसिद्धसाध्यविलक्षणं फलमित्यर्थः») and the seeker («स एवोपेता»). He also gives a second explanation, in which the first phrases ask about meditation and the last about the goal not bounded by time — «कालापरिच्छिन्नमुपेयं पृष्टम्» — and defends it at length.
Śaṅkara: the made is the effect, the unmade the cause — «कृतं कार्यमकृतं कारणम्».

metre.name: anuṣṭubh
metre.note: Anuṣṭubh, 18 + 17 syllables: pādas of 10, 8, 9 and 8. The repeated anyatra lengthens the first and third pādas; every witness has the same words.

beginner: Death has just praised the boy and said the door stands open. Naciketas does not relax. He asks again, more sharply. Tell me, he says, what you see that is beyond right and wrong, beyond what is made and what is not yet made, beyond what has been and what is still to come. Every ordinary thing falls inside these pairs: our actions are good or bad, things are made or not yet made, events belong to the past or the future. The boy wants what lies outside all of them. Śaṅkara says he is asking one thing: what no part of time can measure, and what lies beyond all our dealings. Raṅgarāmānuja, following an earlier teacher of his school, hears three questions in the verse: about the way, the goal and the one who travels. Either way, the request is for something no list of actions could contain.
analogy: Like asking a mapmaker not for one more road, but for the paper the whole map is drawn on.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: He asks Death to tell him what he sees as other than dharma and adharma, other than this made and unmade, other than what has been and what is to be.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Naciketas speaks again, having heard the praise — «एतच्छ्रुत्वा नचिकेताः पुनराह» — if he is fit and Death is pleased. He asks for what is apart from scriptural duty with its fruit and agents, from sin, from effect and cause, and from all three times — «कालत्रयेण यन्न परिच्छिद्यत इत्यर्थः»: a thing beyond the range of all dealing, «सर्वव्यवहारगोचरातीतं».

commentary.q: Raṅgarāmānuja: why the question is asked
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: The verses just spoken said that the goal is reached by knowledge, not by dharma (1.2.10, 1.2.12, 1.2.13); the boy now asks so that the goal, the means and the one who attains may be made clear. Raṅgarāmānuja reports Vyāsārya’s reading under Brahmasūtra 1.4.6: dharma stands for the means, «धर्मः उपायः», and the means asked about is unlike the familiar ones, «प्रसिद्धोपायविलक्षण उपायः इत्यर्थः»; adharma stands for the goal, a fruit unlike familiar fruits, «प्रसिद्धसाध्यविलक्षणं फलमित्यर्थः»; ‘this’ is the seeker, «स एवोपेता».

commentary.label: comparative
commentary.text: Śaṅkara hears one question, which restates the third boon. Raṅgarāmānuja, with Vyāsārya and Brahmasūtra 1.4.6 (‘and so the mention and the question are of three only’), hears the means, the goal and the attainer, and defends the reading against the objection that the four anyatra phrases must describe a single thing. Madhva’s bhāṣya on the passage 1.2.14–17 consists of one verse he cites without naming its source («इति च»), about the imperishable of 1.2.16–17.

advaita.text: One thing is asked: what no time bounds — «कालत्रयेण यन्न परिच्छिद्यत इत्यर्थः» — and what lies beyond all dealing.

visistadvaita.text: Three things are asked — the means, the goal and the seeker — on Vyāsārya’s reading: «धर्मः उपायः» … «स एवोपेता».

schools.disagreement: Whether the verse asks one question (Śaṅkara) or three (Raṅgarāmānuja, after Vyāsārya). Madhva’s bhāṣya on the passage 1.2.14–17 consists of one verse he cites without naming its source («इति च»), about the imperishable of 1.2.16–17.

parallels.note: ‘The mention and the question are of three only’: Raṅgarāmānuja reports Vyāsārya’s reading of this verse under the sūtra.
The Māṇḍūkya speaks of what is ‘beyond the three times’; Śaṅkara’s gloss on this verse makes the same point.

contemporary.text: Most of a working life is spent inside the pairs this verse names: right and wrong decisions, things built and not yet built, last quarter and next. Naciketas asks for what lies outside all of them. A leader need not answer that question to gain from asking it: it is a reminder that the scorecard is not the whole of what matters. This is a reflection, not a claim made by the text.

reflect.beginner: Is there anything about you that is not past, not future, and not something you did or failed to do?
reflect.deeper: Why might the boy press his question just when he has been praised?
reflect.practice: For one day, notice how often your thoughts are about the past or the future, and how often about now.

flags.note: One question (Śaṅkara) or three — means, goal, attainer (Raṅgarāmānuja, after Vyāsārya).
